cases.title: A new pipe joins the only pit at its end
cases.plan_item: UX-PIPE-02 (daily case D03), the start-on-a-pit half only
cases.expected: CD draws a pipe from the new pit P8; the command line says 'Inserted flow arrow. Flow: P8 -> Open end' and 'End is free: open end flagged, connect it later.' once (the far end is free by design); exactly one new pipe object and one new pit; the pipe's own data is read back (record); the line never says the flow starts from an open end (the BUG-560 drift). A twin of this case that starts the pipe 2 m away from the pit must NOT say 'Flow: P8' (R02_BROKEN, the red).
cases.why_not_unit: The join is made by the live CD point landing against the real pit in the drawing.
not_automated: (batch 3 fixes, 25 Oct 2026) Pit Schedule row P8 (D03 assertion 3): the schedule is opened, its cells read as text (R38 route) and closed with its Close button; the row must hold the outlet IL 18.00 and the diameter 225. The other end of a pipe is in the twin case R02b.
The other end: a pipe whose SECOND end lands on a pit is not covered (UX-PIPE-02 says either end). This case counts for 'a pipe started on a pit joins it' only.
BUG-560 (a pipe picked by CLICKING a pit body) is not proved: this case types the pit centre, which BUG-560's own update says worked.

The pit outline and the pipe's first vertex are not read: ent-read of a pipe object returns only its handle, object and layer (probe 25 Oct 2026). The join is proved by CE's own command line ('Flow: P8 -> Open end') plus the pipe's box corner (CE moves the pipe end to the pit wall, so the lower-left corner of the pipe box sits 225 mm right of the pit centre: x 150225, y -80112.5, tolerance 50 mm; a pipe started 2 m away cannot sit there).

cases.plan_item: UX-PIPE-02 (daily case D03), the pipe-ends-on-a-pit half

Flow: Open end -> P8' once, makes exactly one new pipe object, and the pipe box sits at y -80112.5 like the pipe that leaves the pit. cases.title: PIT and CD keep placing until Esc, Esc keeps what was placed, and one U takes back only the last pipe
cases.expected: PIT places a first pit, offers the next, takes a second pit; CD places a first pipe, offers the next, takes a second pipe; each Esc ends it with the 'Stopped' line and keeps what was placed: 2 new pits on layer STORMWATER PIT, 2 new pipe objects, 2 flow arrows, 4 IL texts (18.000, 17.900, 17.800, 17.700) and 2 pipe labels; no New Pit or New Pipe window is left open; the Civil log says 'Command outcome: PIT completed' and 'Command outcome: CD completed' and never 'cancelled' for either; ONE U takes back only the last pipe with its two IL texts, its label and its arrow, leaves both pits and the first pipe.
cases.why_not_unit: The run is a chain of real AutoCAD command instances queued one behind another. Only live AutoCAD shows that the next pick really places another object, what Esc keeps and what one U takes back.
not_automated: The second pit and the second pipe are placed with the real mouse (typed text is lost while CE waits at a prompt). The second pipe's length is not asserted (its label read 1 IN 54 in probe PRH1: the click point is not the exact typed point).
The pit label block and the text sizes are not judged (a look item for Codex).
